expectation: Membrane ring stain on scattered lymphocytes. In gut these are intraepithelial lymphocytes sitting between epithelial cells at the crypt and villus base, plus tissue-resident memory CD8 T cells in the lamina propria. Expect a subset of CD8a+ cells, as discrete small round cells, with a few dendritic cells.
notes: CD103 looks like a haze over the tissue and the glass, with ribbons along the crypt and epithelial edges. It does not mark discrete cells. CD8a clearly shows cells, yet those cells are mostly CD103-negative and the CD103 bands run past them.
observed: A: yellow haze over all the tissue and the glass, bright streaks in muscle folds, debris dots. B: diffuse streaks. C: a bright speckled rim round a gland lumen. D: blurry blobs with no ring-shaped cells. E: CD8a shows crisp cells, while CD103 forms continuous ribbons along epithelial outlines that mostly miss the magenta cells.
why: CD103 follows the tissue's texture and epithelial outlines as continuous bands, not discrete membrane-stained cells, and it mostly misses the clearly stained CD8a+ cells.
